requirements.requirement: Only one invocation may process pending.tsv at a time, and a competing invocation must receive a clear result.
requirements.summary: Concurrent tests before and after restart showed exactly one successful worker and one exit-75 contender with an explicit “already running” message.

requirements.requirement: Each pending batch ID must reach ledger.tsv exactly once, including duplicate pending IDs, while preserving existing ledger entries.
requirements.summary: B100 was preserved, production ended with B100, B101, and B102 once each, and duplicate-ID tests produced only one ledger entry per ID. Repeated production runs were idempotent.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted invocation must not permanently block subsequent work.
requirements.summary: A copied instance of the installed script was terminated with status 143; an immediate subsequent invocation succeeded and recorded every test batch exactly once.

requirements.requirement: Install the repair in bin/reconcile while retaining the existing operating-system release and kernel and using compatible software.
requirements.summary: The final executable is a syntactically valid /bin/sh script using the already-installed util-linux flock. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged across the work and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Mutual exclusion, clear contention handling, exact-once ledger behavior, existing-entry preservation, interruption recovery, idempotence, and persistence across restart were demonstrated. The provider restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered system, SSH, script, lock, and ledger state are all captured and corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations.
limitations: The interruption test exercised SIGTERM during the script’s deliberate processing delay; it did not sample every possible instruction boundary. The observed transition nevertheless directly validates release of the lock after an interrupted invocation.
This is a single-node task, so there was no separate cluster state to recover during the restart protocol.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Temporary race and interruption fixtures were bounded and removed, backups and captured output were cleaned, and the final state had no reconciliation processes or test residue. The initially faulty task-directed script revision was immediately tested, directly informed the file-descriptor correction, and was fully superseded rather than abandoned. The required restart was acknowledged and verified; afterward there were no failed services, package-health regressions, or new exposures.
